answer_md:
🐾 Here’s what Matt has built, changed, and delivered.

Matt’s work spans Execution & Delivery, Org & Working-Model Transformation, and Talent & Enablement. At **Capital One**, slow, misaligned product iterations extended time-to-market and disconnected solutions from user needs. At **Norfolk Southern**, orders fell out of a decades-old mainframe system unnoticed until customers called, while account leadership expected waterfall delivery. At **Accenture**, expanding modern product engineering meant recruiting and developing practitioners who often lacked hands-on cloud-native or Agile experience. The work required changing both the software and how teams built it.

At **Capital One**, Matt brought product, design, and engineering into a balanced team of **8**. He introduced a value-prioritized, testable backlog, pair programming, and disciplined test-driven development: write a failing test, write minimal code to pass it, then safely refactor. The team delivered features **3 to 4 times faster** than other **Accenture** teams on the same engagement, with **zero production defects**. The client sought to retain the team beyond the planned end.

At **Norfolk Southern**, Matt led modernization without stopping the railroad. The mainframe remained the system of record while APIs, microservices, and CockroachDB rose beside it, with change data capture and reconciliation validating the systems against each other. He brought revenue management into co-creation and weekly build-measure-learn iterations. The MVP launched covering **95% of its targeted use cases**, capturing real orders with clean data feeding the mainframe. Client contributors paired into the build, learning the technologies needed to support the application after **Accenture** rolled off.

Matt also built **Accenture’s** Atlanta and Tampa Cloud Innovation Centers from **0 to 150+ practitioners**, owning full P&L accountability, hiring, training, and career development. The centers delivered **30+ product engagements** across **15+ Fortune 500 clients**. Teams achieved **4X faster velocity** and zero-defect deployments through TDD and automated pipelines. Delivery excellence and customer relationships generated **\$100M+ in repeat business**.

question: Does he have a CS degree?

answer_md:
🐾 Here’s the work behind the degree.

Matt holds a Master's degree in Information Technology from **American InterContinental University**. Information Technology is a recognized Computer Science-related discipline. If your requirement is specifically a degree titled “Computer Science,” his degree has a different title.

If your concern is what technical work he has actually done, at **AT&T**, the Network Engineer implementation needed integration agreements and detailed technical designs before downstream development could proceed. Matt defined Joint Interface Agreements for MIC, MIC-NT, and ELP, designed enhancements using .NET, C#, SQL Server, and ESRI APIs, and conducted technical and functional reviews of offshore-delivered code. The agreements unblocked **3** integration points, and enhancements delivered without architectural rework between phases.

At **Accenture**, engineers were struggling to adopt cloud-native technologies without standardized resources. Rather than relying only on training, Matt led Project Octane: reusable reference applications, infrastructure-as-code templates, automated provisioning with Terraform and AWS CloudFormation, and hands-on workshops. The reference applications included Summit, using AWS AppSync for real-time GraphQL sync backed by ElastiCache.

His own MattGPT project also accumulated technical debt during rapid prototyping. Matt separated pages, services, and utilities, scoped CSS, and tested each extraction locally before deploying and verifying it in production. He reduced the main application file from **5,765** to **1,014** lines, an **82%** reduction, and documented the changes through **12** atomic Git commits and architectural decision records.
